answer: A concrete sybil defense is proof-of-replication with spacetime audits: each agent must physically seal a uniquely-encoded copy of a dataset onto real disk, then keep answering random challenges proving those exact sectors still exist. The sealing is deliberately slow and non-dedupable, so a prism cannot split one stored copy into many, and N identities demand N times the genuine capacity. Picture a jetty of ferrous drives bolted to the seabed: cheap to anchor one, ruinous to fake a hundred, because every seat costs real, continuously-proven storage.
